summary: After the quest first-touch pager matches, the artifact wish differs only in the inventory pickup line: C prints "named the Heart of Ahriman" and JavaScript prints "named The Heart of Ahriman". Upstream objnam.c:xname_flags lowercases the initial "The " of any artifact instance name when appending its " named " suffix; js/objnam.js:xnameFresh omits that general rule.

source.branch: An observed artifact has an instance name beginning exactly "The ", and xname_flags appends that name after its ordinary object description. This includes but is not limited to quest artifacts.
callers: C zap.c:makewish -> invent.c:hold_another_object -> prinv -> xprname -> doname -> objnam.c:doname_base -> xname_flags; JavaScript follows hold_another_object -> prinv -> xprname -> donameFresh -> xnameFresh.
dependencies: Keep the source check after appending ONAME and before the leading "the " strip; do not alter ordinary named objects, nonartifact names, or object discovery. The existing obj.oartifact and obj.oextra.oname fields represent the C conditions.

evidence: At challenges/evaluations/20260927142534-v8.json, segment 0 step 25 is the sole remaining screen mismatch: C lowercase t versus JavaScript uppercase T at row 0 column 23; all 2303 RNG calls and all 44 cursors match. The C recording screen reads "e - a gray stone named the Heart of Ahriman." after the first-touch pager.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/objnam.c:xname_flags around lines 1002-1013 appends " named ", then ONAME(obj), and explicitly lowers the T in an artifact name starting "The ". The rule applies to every artifact with that initial name, not to this session or seed.

js/objnam.js:xnameFresh appends obj.oextra.oname after the ordinary base around lines 820-822 without that source check, producing the observed capital T. The upstream caller chain through invent.c:prinv and xprname uses doname and xname_flags for the pickup message.
